issue_context.title: Bluetooth isochronous channels central_iso / peripheral_iso example not working reliable on nrf52840dk – packets not received/lost
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
I tried the two examples: [CENTRAL_ISO](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/main/samples/bluetooth/central_iso) & [PERIPHERAL_ISO](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/tree/main/samples/bluetooth/peripheral_iso)
with two nrf52840, one running central and one running peripheral.

Problem:
Data stream on iso channel stops at some point.

Software flow:
1. Connection is established between central and peripheral.
2. ISO channel is connected succesfully.
3. Central starts data stream (all parameters from example left unchanged)
4. Peripheral receives some data and prints messages to console.
5. At some point (after few intervals) the peripheral is not receiving any more data, while central is still "sending".

I can extend data stream duration by increasing the channel interval.

 - What target platform are you using?
 nRF52840

 - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue?
I checked with Segger's Systemview and saw that the BT TX thread is called periodically on the central, but the BT RX thread is not called on the peripheral after data reception has stopped.


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Flash CENTRAL_ISO and PERIPHERAL_ISO to two seperate nrf52840DK Boards
2. Let them execute the app and observe received data on peripheral
3. See that no more data arrives after a certain point in time

**Expected behavior**
Reliable data stream on the Bluetooth LE Isochronous channel between the two devices.

**Impact**
As it works using the nRF Connect SDK 2.6.0 (SoftDevice Controller), this can be used as an alternative.

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ea995f6378f7f6a6f8b6b1f7df29e0af7437f7a1/samples/bluetooth/broadcast_audio_source/overlay-bt_ll_sw_split.conf#L17-L24

Host or Controller does not need any fix, the comment about fixing host should be removed? @Thalley ?

> https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ea995f6378f7f6a6f8b6b1f7df29e0af7437f7a1/samples/bluetooth/broadcast_audio_source/overlay-bt_ll_sw_split.conf#L17-L24
>

As discussed previously I do think something needs to change so that `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_ISO_TX_BUFFER_SIZE` can default to `CONFIG_BT_ISO_TX_MTU` (or even just use `CONFIG_BT_ISO_TX_MTU` in the controller). In my mind that makes the most sense. 


@rugeGerritsen You may also have some input here

> > Some samples have the below comment, but maybe the right thing is to have the increased bytes in the Controller's CONFIG_BT_CTLR_ISO_TX_BUFFER_SIZE` as done in this sample:
> > https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/ea995f6378f7f6a6f8b6b1f7df29e0af7437f7a1/samples/bluetooth/broadcast_audio_source/overlay-bt_ll_sw_split.conf#L17-L24
> > 
> > Host or Controller does not need any fix, the comment about fixing host should be removed? @Thalley ?
> 
> As discussed previously I do think something needs to change so that `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_ISO_TX_BUFFER_SIZE` can default to `CONFIG_BT_ISO_TX_MTU` (or even just use `CONFIG_BT_ISO_TX_MTU` in the controller). In my mind that makes the most sense.
> 
> @rugeGerritsen You may also have some input here

This sounds like a good idea. The SoftDevice controller uses the MTU size for configuring memory buffer sizes: https://github.com/nrfconnect/sdk-nrf/blob/main/subsys/bluetooth/controller/hci_driver.c#L1104

Note: `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_ISO_TX_BUFFER_SIZE` needs to be set to `CONFIG_BT_ISO_TX_MTU + 8` if you want to support sending HCI ISO packets with timestamp to the controller. The `8` corresponds to the ISO SDU header and timestamp size.
This is only one of several issues in the ISO central sample, see #72452. I'll provide fixes shortly.

review_comments:
I see what you are trying to do here, and I agree the naming could be improved. 

What I'm worried about here is that these are not headers for SDUs, but SDU fragments. 

If the host sends an SDU in 3 fragments to the controller, this header will appear 3 times. 

Would `bt_hci_iso_sdu_frag_xx` be better?

Will it though?
I think those "headers" are really part of the whole-sdu payload. Just like the SDU "header" in L2CAP K-frames, they shouldn't be repeated for every fragment. It's only there at the start of the SDU, so the first HCI fragment.

I would however be ok with renaming `struct bt_hci_iso_hdr` to `struct bt_hci_iso_data_hdr`:
![image](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/68428270/0d8b8e27-70ac-4d93-a0f5-dfa37214f088)

> What I'm worried about here is that these are not headers for SDUs, but SDU fragments.

I disagree here, by the Spec:

```
If PB_Flag equals 0b00 or 0b10, then the Packet_Sequence_Number,
ISO_SDU_Length, and Packet_Status_Flag fields (plus the intermediate RFU
field) shall all be present in the packet and the Time_Stamp field may be
present. If PB_Flag equals 0b01 or 0b11, then none of these fields shall be
included in the packet.
```

Hence, `struct bt_hci_iso_sdu_hdr` is once per SDU (first fragment or complete SDU) from the upper layer, these fields are not part of next SDU fragment towards the Controller.

> I would however be ok with renaming struct bt_hci_iso_hdr to struct bt_hci_iso_data_hdr

This I can do, and will be closer to the Spec wording `HCI ISO Data packet header`.

> > What I'm worried about here is that these are not headers for SDUs, but SDU fragments.
> 
> I disagree here, by the Spec:
> 
> ```
> If PB_Flag equals 0b00 or 0b10, then the Packet_Sequence_Number,
> ISO_SDU_Length, and Packet_Status_Flag fields (plus the intermediate RFU
> field) shall all be present in the packet and the Time_Stamp field may be
> present. If PB_Flag equals 0b01 or 0b11, then none of these fields shall be
> included in the packet.
> ```
> 
> Hence, `struct bt_hci_iso_sdu_hdr` is once per SDU (first fragment or complete SDU) from the upper layer, these fields are not part of next SDU fragment towards the Controller.

I stand corrected. Thanks! 

In this case, I'm OK with the new naming
super confusing as always from the SIG. And the next bit in the same paragraph is cool too "SDU fragments generated over HCI are unrelated to the SDU fragments generated by ISOAL".
Indeed. The entire ISO over HCI is a complete mess :(
